task_completion.visual_evidence: Screenshots showing the agent clicking on and viewing at least 5 different patent detail pages (e.g., USXXXXXXX).

task_completion.visual_evidence: Firefox bookmark menu or sidebar showing a new folder with the exact name 'Patent Landscape Research'.

task_completion.visual_evidence: Firefox bookmark manager or dropdown showing 5 patent URLs/titles inside the 'Patent Landscape Research' folder.

task_completion.visual_evidence: A text editor or file manager showing the file 'patent_landscape.json' exists in the Documents folder.

integrity.description: The agent interacted with the web interface rather than just generating a file from internal knowledge.
integrity.visual_evidence: Screenshots must show active navigation, scrolling, or clicking on the Google Patents/USPTO websites.

integrity.description: The agent did not use terminal commands to 'touch' or 'echo' the bookmarks into Firefox's internal database files directly.
integrity.visual_evidence: The agent is seen using the Firefox GUI (right-click, star icon, or bookmark menu) to add bookmarks.

integrity.description: The patent numbers in the JSON report match the patents actually visited in the browser.
integrity.visual_evidence: The patent numbers visible in the browser tabs/address bars match the 'patent_number' values in the final JSON file.

privileged_info_for_vlm: Verified US utility patents for this topic include US8193764B2 and US9356659B2. Valid US patent numbers typically follow the format 'US' followed by 7-11 digits (e.g., US9356659). Grant dates must be in YYYY-MM-DD format. The bookmark folder name must be exactly 'Patent Landscape Research'. Relevant CPC codes often start with H02J (e.g., H02J50/10 for inductive charging).
